texts.facts: The petitioners are aggrieved against the proceedings of the third respondent dated 27.12.2018 and 28.12.2018, cancelling the licenses issued under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 to carry on the business of selling sweets and bakery items at No.78, Sitco Near, Thirumalai Thirupathy Nagar, Kachirapalayam Road, Kallakurichi, Villupuram District and to carry on the business of preparing sweets and bakery items at Srivasavi Sweets and Backery Preparation Centre- 1, No.78, Sitco Near, Thirumalai Thirupathy Nagar, Kachirapalayam Road, Kallakurichi, Villupuram District 606 202 and Srivasavi Sweets and Backery Preparation Centre-2, No.76/8A, Sitco Near, Thirumalai Srivasavi Sweets And Backery vs The State Of Tamil Nadu on 14 March, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100560946/ 3 http://www.judis.nic.in Thirupathy Nagar, Kachirapalayam Road, Kallakurichi, Villupuram District 606 202. Consequently, the petitioner seek for a direction to the respondents 1 to 3 to carry on the business at the above said premises. 3.It is seen that the petitioners were running a sweet cum bakery stall in the name and style of Srivasavi Sweets and Backery at No.78, Sitco Near, Thirumalai Thirupathy Nagar, Kachirapalayam Road, Kallakurichi, Villupuram District and for preparing sweets and bakery items they had two preparation centres both in Thirumalai Thirupathy Nagar, Kachirapalayam Road, Kallakurichi, Villupuram District at different door numbers. 4. It is seen that by proceedings dated 21.12.2018, the Commissioner of Kallakurichy Municipality sealed the preparation centres in Thirumalai Thirupathy Nagar, Kachirapalayam Road, Kallakurichi, Villupuram District at different door numbers on the http://www.judis.nic.in reason that the same was being run without any permission and against the public safety. The said order was challenged before this Court in W.P.No.34666 of 2018. The Writ Court by order dated 28.12.2018 dismissed the writ petition. Challenging the said order, the writ petitioner filed writ appeal in W.A.No.234 of 2019. , we find that the appellant submitted an application before the second respondent much earlier and not after the writ petition was disposed of.
